title: Two random lines: do they track?
hook: Two lines, each driven by its own coin flips. Could they still move together?

knows: correlation as two things moving together
doesNotKnow: that trending random series correlate by chance
that independent random walks often look related

misconception: Two unrelated lines that track each other must share a cause.
objective: The learner can say that two independent random walks have |r| above 0.5 about 40% of the time, so tracking lines are not evidence of a shared cause.
keyState: At least 41 seeded pairs drawn (on the click path 17 of 41 have |r| above 0.5; strongest r = +0.88).

claims.text: Each line is a random walk of 100 steps, each step +1 or -1 by a fair coin flip, and the two lines never influence each other.
claims.source: model.ts pair(): alternating mulberry32 draws for the two walks.

claims.text: Over 100,000 seeded pairs of independent 100-step walks, 39.8% have a correlation r with |r| above 0.5.
claims.source: strongShare(100000, 1000000) in model.ts: pairs seeded mulberry32(1000000 + i), r over the 101 points of each walk (recomputed in node, 0.3979). Brief's earlier 39.7% is consistent within sampling error (about 0.15 percentage points).

claims.text: In the pairs on the stage, 17 of the first 41 have |r| above 0.5, and the strongest has r = +0.88.
claims.source: Pair i uses mulberry32(5000 + i), untuned (first seed tried). Over 300 other seed sets of 41 pairs the strong count averaged 15.9 (range 6 to 24), so 17 is typical; the first 11 pairs have only 2 strong (expected about 4).

claims.text: Random walks drift in slow trends, so two independent ones often rise or fall together by accident (spurious correlation).
claims.source: Known as spurious regression: Yule, G. U. (1926), J. Royal Statistical Society 89: 1-63; Granger, C. W. J. & Newbold, P. (1974), J. Econometrics 2: 111-120. Wording to be checked against the papers.

claims.text: Lines that track each other do not prove a shared cause.
claims.source: Follows from claim 2: independent walks have |r| > 0.5 about 40% of the time.

recall.question: Two independent random walks are plotted over 100 steps. About how often will they look strongly correlated (|r| above 0.5)?
recall.why: Each walk drifts in slow trends, so two of them line up by accident about 40% of the time.
